what: Example 1: A binary educational test, verifying Lord (1955)
title: Worked examples
text: dichotomous case, absolute CSEM derived Generalizability Theory single-facet p×ip \times design collapses Lord’s (1955) classic binomial-error formula. Letting XpX_p denote person pp’s observed total raw score nin_i number items, σ̂(Δp)=1niXp(ni−Xp)ni−1. \hat{\sigma}(\Delta_p) \;=\; \frac{1}{n_i}\sqrt{\frac{X_p(n_i - X_p)}{n_i - 1}}. Brennan (1998) makes equivalence explicit (equation 8). verify numerically iowa_like, simulated ITED-Vocabulary-like dataset distributed package; see ?iowa_like calibration details. keep example fast work reproducible subsample 600 persons. package returns one fitted value per observed total score fit$by_score. compare Lord formula evaluated scores: maximum absolute discrepancy floor double precision; two formulas algebraically identical binary p×ip \times design. Per-person absolute CSEM iowa_like subsample (n = 600, = 40), full estimator.

what: D-study: projecting to a different test length
title: Worked examples
text: Generalizability Theory projects precision test alternative test lengths via D-study (Brennan, 2001). csem_gt() controlled n_items_D: passing value different observed number items rescales error variances reliability coefficients hypothetical length, G-study variance components remain fixed. csem_gt projection Spearman-Brown predicted reliability agree closely. small remaining differences reflect way GT treats item-variance term, Spearman-Brown’s classical derivation assumes away. longer tests values converge asymptote.

text: csemGT estimates conditional standard errors measurement (CSEMs) Generalizability Theory univariate single-facet design persons crossed items (p $\times$ design).
